# Implementation

## Stack ownership

Preserve the maintained stack and adopted components. Read runtime, lockfile, rendering/routing,
deployment, and token evidence together; one filename does not establish ownership. A visual
request does not authorize a runtime or styling migration. When stack choice is genuinely open,
eliminate options that cannot meet the required rendering, distribution, platform APIs, access,
or maintenance constraints. Compare credible survivors on the hardest real path, including
state/data ownership and reversal cost; a library's look or demo size is not decisive evidence.

## Platform adaptation

Adapt platform behavior, not just its pixels: navigation and Back, text scaling, focus/input,
safe areas, system preferences, and materials follow the target's maintained components.
CSS pixels and relative units, native points, and density/scalable units are not interchangeable.
Test the actual target, enlarged text, supported inputs, and effective system preferences.
Sharing content and domain rules does not require identical chrome or physical measurements.

For target behavior, read `platforms.md`; for delivered email and host boundaries, `email.md`;
for spatial representation and derivative delivery, `3d.md`.

## Component and styling ownership

Choose ownership before vendor names: native controls retain platform behavior; headless packages
own primitives while the product owns presentation; styled packages also own visual defaults;
copied source makes the local maintainer responsible for updates and divergence. Custom behavior
owns all those costs. Prove fit on the hardest actual dialog, date field or data task, including
localization, input-method composition, keyboard/focus, server rendering and relevant themes.
A composed product can break an accessible primitive; a button demo proves no assembled contract.

Keep one coherent styling authority. Compare authored static CSS, local scoping, build-time
utilities/extraction and runtime styles by actual rendering, theming and maintenance needs, not
syntax brevity. Generate repeated values from the canonical semantic source. Inspect emitted CSS
and dependency resolution before assuming a shared package leaves global styles to the consumer.
Public tokens are not the same contract as internal variables.

Declare layer/import ownership before chasing specificity. For normal author declarations,
unlayered styles outrank layered styles; class order does not reverse that. Verify a cold direct
visit and client navigation in production output when lazy chunks can change order. A font
variable neither loads nor applies its face: inspect winning longhands/shorthands and rendered
fallbacks. `lps-system` owns effective theme selection, token graphs and conversion.

## Stateful implementation

Keep attempts, dismissal requests and confirmed completion distinct. Failed validation/save
preserves the draft and error; a requested close does not prove success. Read the installed
primitive's event/cancellation contract rather than assuming payloads survive an adapter.
Resize an open dialog into its narrow presentation and verify input, focus, scroll and dismissal.
CSS can adapt presentation without replacing state identity; an initial server fallback is not
knowledge of the eventual viewport and does not prove hydration or focus stability.

Use native semantics before rebuilding their behavior. Preserve tabular relationships, sort
state and task-required filter/history behavior; do not automatically turn comparison rows into
cards or virtualize from source shape alone. Existing `lps-ux` references own recovery semantics.

## SVG reuse and embedding

Reuse exact approved artwork or the governed icon family's glyph before drawing a local diagram
or genuinely missing concept. Do not reconstruct a known mark, trace an unapproved illustration,
or replace a whole interface with one SVG. The surrounding HTML/native controls retain reflow,
selection and behavior; the vector carries only its proper graphic job.

Choose embedding by trust, semantics, theming and caching: trusted inline artwork enters the DOM;
an image has a text alternative but cannot inherit page styles internally; a background carries
no required content; a controlled sprite needs reference/ID checks. A document embed is active
content, not the image context. Untrusted markup follows the existing security pipeline, never
direct inline injection or a new sanitizer created for this reference.

Preserve viewBox, aspect, notices and dimensions. Glyph size is separate from the interactive
target. Namespace internal references and exercise several instances, including stable
server/client IDs; optimization can break gradients, masks and semantic references. Review
script/event/foreign content and external references under the existing policy. Image isolation
is neither legal clearance nor proof of upload safety.
